partners.mechanism_chain: RET (HGNC:9916) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP450); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP450) —INCREASES→ MAPK cascade (WP:WP111); MAPK cascade (WP:WP111) —LEADS_TO→ Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma (MONDO:0007958); PIK3R1 (HGNC:9520) —DECREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP450); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP450) —LEADS_TO→ SHORT syndrome (MONDO:0010026). Gain-of-function mutations in RET lead to constitutive activation of the PI3K-Akt signaling pathway, which in turn activates downstream effectors like the MAPK cascade, contributing to familial medullary thyroid carcinoma. While the exact downstream effects leading to SHORT syndrome are complex, dysregulation of this central pathway is a common link.

Gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene lead to the development of medullary thyroid carcinoma. RET signaling can also impinge upon the MTOR pathway. Aberrant activation of the MTOR signaling pathway, potentially influenced by RET or other upstream activators, is a known mechanism for various cerebral malformations, including 'obsolete cerebral malformation'.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that RET signaling does not influence MTOR pathway activity in relevant cell types, or that mutations in MTOR pathway components are absent in patients with obsolete cerebral malformation. _(variant: rs1800888 (RET V600E) with an allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD.)_
